evidence: Receiving DO2: 12.1 mg/L at t=48.0h, then 7.75 mg/L at 48.2h and monotonic decline to 6.94 mg/L at t=52.0h (online sensor series)
Delayed assay P=2.82 g/L at t=48h, confirming active production phase and elevated OUR
Source batches 1-3 show normal DO2 (8-14 mg/L) sustained through 48-96h, isolating the receiving-side oxygen deficit
Allowed action bounds: increase_air = [1.0, 1.15] aeration multiplier, well below any oxygen-constraint risk; feed-preserving vs reduce_feed/strong_feed_reduction
DO2 minimum constraint 2.0 mg/L
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 shows a distinct step-down at ~48h (12.1 -> 7.8 mg/L) with continued slow decline to 6.9 mg/L at the 52h decision point, while product assays confirm the culture is in high-growth, high-OUR production. Source reference batches never show such a drop. A bounded +15% aeration increase directly restores oxygen transfer capacity, keeps DO2 well above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, and preserves full feed so product mass is retained. Feed reductions were rejected to avoid product loss; stop was rejected as zero production.
submission.uncertainty: Moderate: hidden OUR kinetics and oxygen-transfer coefficients are unknown, so the exact DO2 recovery magnitude is uncertain; however, the large margin above the 2.0 mg/L limit and the monotonic decline justify a conservative aeration boost. If the decline were sensor-related rather than a true OUR/transfer deficit, the intervention is still safe (bounded +15%) and low-regret.
